public_rationale: Contemporaneous developer disclosures and independent testing show that safety-trained LLMs could still produce harmful outputs when prompted in particular ways. OpenAI reported meaningful improvements, but explicitly acknowledged remaining failures. This supports the ordinary reading that consistent adherence remained a substantial technical challenge.
limitations: The evidence concerns GPT-4 and ChatGPT, not every LLM or every possible ethical framework.
The independent study was a preprint and does not give an exact testing date in its abstract.
This establishes a practical reliability problem, not a proof that alignment is impossible.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Getting LLMs to consistently align with any set of ethical values is a major unsolved challenge.

statement.excerpt: Another major challenge lies in forcing LLMs to consistently align with (any) set of ethical values.
statement.document_title: How China might crush the West in the race to AGI if we don’t up our regulatory game

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that reliable adherence to specified ethical rules remained a substantial technical problem for contemporary general-purpose LLMs.
The parenthetical does not assert that every conceivable rule set is impossible to satisfy. It emphasizes the difficulty of reliable adherence even after values have been specified.
Because there is no regular reporting period for model capabilities, the target is the current public state documented during early 2023 through the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary evaluations or developer disclosures show that safety-trained LLMs could still be induced to violate their stated ethical or safety rules.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, credible evaluations demonstrate reliable adherence to specified ethical rules, including under adversarial prompting, sufficient to show that this was no longer a substantial unresolved problem.

evidence.locator: Risks & mitigations, paragraph following the safety-improvement discussion
evidence.explanation: OpenAI acknowledged that its launched model could still violate behavioral safeguards after mitigation. The same disclosure reports substantial improvements, which qualify the severity but do not establish consistent adherence.

evidence.locator: Abstract, following the finding about persona-induced toxicity
evidence.explanation: The authors report testing more than half a million ChatGPT generations and finding that persona assignments increased harmful and discriminatory outputs. This independently supports a practical failure of reliable safety adherence.
